newsitem.title: FRANCE: TOTAL SAYS IN TALKS WITH ASHLAND.
newsitem.headline: TOTAL SAYS IN TALKS WITH ASHLAND.

text.p: French oil company Total said on Monday it was in talks with Ashland about concession rights in Nigeria which the military government revoked in June.
"Total is talking with Ashland to protect our interests on the 90225 block," a Total spokesman said.
The spokesman declined to comment on whether Total was negotiating with the Nigerian government to acquire Ashland's concession rights.
Nigerian newspapers reported on Monday that Total was close to a deal to acquire those rights.
"We have no comment on what is said in Nigerian newspapers," the spokesman said.
Nigeria's military government recently named an eight-man committee to manage the affairs of the local unit of Ashland whose operating licence was revoked in June.
Nigeria cancelled Ashland's licence after it was discovered the company wanted to sell its contract licence, interests and rights to France's privately-held Perenco Investment S.A.
Under a production sharing contract, the operating company wholly finances exploration of a project and reaps the profits if oil is struck.
Ashland had been pumping some 20,000 barrels daily from the concession.
